advances: For an explicit graphical reduced-core class, this proves the original-law bound \(M_3(p)\ge 8^{-n}/4096\) and an actual original root of normalized closed-halfspace depth at least \(2^{-n}/16\), uniformly in all tilts. The class allows arbitrarily many dense components with arbitrarily different degree scales, arbitrarily many independent cycle components, arbitrary finite subdivisions and tree attachments, and unbounded cycle rank. All dense components are estimated together with one coefficient \(1/64\), and all free loops are estimated together with another coefficient \(1/64\); neither coefficient is charged per component or coordinate. Exact reduction and chart transfer preserve the original total capacity \(T\) and the capacity moment \(T^4M_3(p)\). This is a theorem for the stated graphical class, not the locked weak Oertel theorem or a representation theorem for all mixed-integer convex bodies.

proof:
First suppose \(G_D\ne\varnothing\). For each of its components set \(N_C:=|E(C)|\), \(r_C:=|V(C)|-1\), and \(d_v:=\deg_C(v)=\deg_{G_D}(v)\) for \(v\in V(C)\). The handshake identity gives \(2N_C=\sum_{v\in V(C)}d_v\ge m_C|V(C)|\). Hence \(N_C\ge512|V(C)|>r_C\). Summing gives \(N_D\ge1\), \(r_D=\sum_Cr_C<N_D\), and \(n_D=\sum_C(N_C-r_C)>0\). Thus all incidence, nonisolated-vertex, and positive-cycle-rank hypotheses of accepted fact 95b42d5db781cc1e hold for the whole graph \(G_D\).

Here is the exact notation map for that application of accepted fact 95b42d5db781cc1e. Its \((G,V,E,N,r,n,\widehat A,A,\boldsymbol\theta,D,Q,p)\) are \((G_D,V_D,E_D,N_D,r_D,n_D,\widehat A_D,A_D,\boldsymbol\theta_D,D_D,Q_D,p_D)\), where \(A_D\) omits one vertex row per component and has the same kernel as \(\widehat A_D\). Its degrees \(d_v\) are the degrees just defined. Its \(\tau_p,M_3\) are \(\tau_{p_D},M_3(p_D)\), with unchanged actual-depth and cubic-moment normalization. Write
\[
R_{G_D}:=\prod_{v\in V_D}(2d_v+1),
\qquad
F_C:=\frac{(2N_C)!}{(2N_C)^{2N_C}}
\prod_{v\in V(C)}\frac{d_v^{d_v}}{d_v!}.
\]
Thus \(R_{G_D}\) is its \(R_G\), \(F_C\) is its \(F_G\) evaluated on the component \(C\), and its \(F_G^{\mathrm{comp}}\) is \(\prod_C F_C\).

Apply inequality (1) of accepted fact 95b42d5db781cc1e once to the whole union, using its permitted replacement (2). This gives
\[
M_3(p_D)\ge
\frac{(25/162)^{N_D}}{64R_{G_D}^6}\prod_C F_C.
\tag{1}
\]
No global degree-balance hypothesis is needed for this inequality. We do not apply that fact's final dense consequence (4) to \(G_D\), nor do we multiply its component moment bounds.

For clarity about the original probability in (1), let \(D_C\) denote the ternary circulation support on \(C\). Incidence constraints of different components involve disjoint edge sets, so
\[
D_D=\prod_C D_C,
\qquad
Q_D=\prod_C\left(\sum_{\mathbf x_C\in D_C}
 e^{(\boldsymbol\theta_D|_{E(C)})\cdot\mathbf x_C}\right).
\tag{2}
\]
These are exact factorizations of the original section and its partition. In particular \(p_D\) is the true product of the component exponential section laws. Inequality (1) concerns its actual ambient caps, not caps of a conditional reflected law or of an auxiliary law.

We now sum elementary component degree budgets. The factorial envelope proved as (18) in accepted fact 95b42d5db781cc1e is
\(\sqrt{2k}(k/e)^k\le k!\le e\sqrt{k}(k/e)^k\) for every integer \(k\ge1\). Apply its lower bound to \((2N_C)!\) and its upper bound to all \(d_v!\). Since \(\sum_{v\in V(C)}d_v=2N_C\), their exponential factors cancel, giving the component version of that fact's envelope (19):
\[
F_C\ge
\frac{\sqrt{4N_C}\,e^{-|V(C)|}}
 {\prod_{v\in V(C)}\sqrt{d_v}}.
\tag{3}
\]
Let \(b:=\log(100/81)=\log(8\cdot25/162)\), exactly the symbol \(b\) in the degree-budget proof of accepted fact 95b42d5db781cc1e. From (1), (3), and \(n_D=\sum_C(N_C-r_C)\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log\bigl(M_3(p_D)8^{n_D}\bigr)
\ge -\log64+\sum_C\Bigl[&N_Cb-r_C\log8
 -6\sum_{v\in V(C)}\log(2d_v+1)\\
&+\tfrac12\log(4N_C)-|V(C)|
 -\tfrac12\sum_{v\in V(C)}\log d_v\Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
This expression has a single \(-\log64\), not one per component.

The elementary integral inequality \(\log(1+x)\ge x/(1+x)\), for \(x\ge0\), gives \(b\ge19/100\) upon taking \(x=19/81\). For each component, use \(N_C\ge m_C|V(C)|/2\), \(r_C\le|V(C)|\), \(2d_v+1\le4m_C+1\), and \(d_v\le2m_C\). Define
\(\psi(x):=19x/200-\log8-1-6\log(4x+1)-\tfrac12\log(2x)\) for \(x\ge1024\). This is exactly the \(\psi\) of the same accepted degree-budget proof, evaluated here separately at each \(m_C\). The bracket for \(C\) in (4) is at least \(|V(C)|\psi(m_C)+\tfrac12\log(4N_C)\).

For completeness, positivity uses the fixed threshold, not a numerical parameter search. For \(x\ge1024\),
\[
\psi'(x)=\frac{19}{200}-\frac{24}{4x+1}-\frac1{2x}
\ge\frac{19}{200}-\frac{13}{2x}>0.
\]
Moreover \(4097<2^{13}\), \(2048=2^{11}\), and \(\log2<1\), so
\[
\psi(1024)>
\frac{19\cdot1024}{200}-3-1-6\cdot13-\frac{11}{2}
=\frac{489}{50}>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus every \(\psi(m_C)\) is positive. Also every \(N_C\ge1\), so every \(\tfrac12\log(4N_C)\) is positive. Summing (4) therefore proves \(\log(M_3(p_D)8^{n_D})\ge-\log64\), or \(M_3(p_D)\ge8^{-n_D}/64\). This argument permits arbitrary differences among the \(m_C\); each component pays its own degree budget inside one whole-union estimate.

Next group all free loops. A loop has zero incidence column, so its coordinate is unconstrained. Consequently, in reduced edge-coordinate order,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_*&=D_D\times\{-1,0,1\}^L,&
Q_*&=Q_DQ_{\mathrm{loop}},\\
p^*_{(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)}&=p_D(\mathbf x)p_{\mathrm{loop}}(\mathbf y),&
\dim\ker\widehat A_*&=n_D+L.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
These are exact identities, including all reduced tilts. If \(L\ge1\), apply accepted fact 84707bfc9d53dbda once to the complete loop group. Its \((N,D,\boldsymbol\theta,p,Z_i)\) are respectively \((L,\{-1,0,1\}^L,\boldsymbol\theta_{\mathrm{loop}},p_{\mathrm{loop}},Z_j)\), with \(i=j\); its depth and moment are exactly \(\tau_{p_{\mathrm{loop}}},M_3(p_{\mathrm{loop}})\). Its inequality (1) yields \(M_3(p_{\mathrm{loop}})\ge8^{-L}/64\). This applies to arbitrary effective loop tilts and any positive \(L\), without a coefficient loss for each loop.

Suppose both groups are nonempty. To transfer these moment estimates to the actual product law, form the probability measures
\[
\mu_D:=\sum_{\mathbf x\in D_D}p_D(\mathbf x)\delta_{\mathbf x}
\quad\text{on }\mathbb R^{E_D},
\qquad
\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}:=\sum_{\mathbf y\in\{-1,0,1\}^L}
 p_{\mathrm{loop}}(\mathbf y)\delta_{\mathbf y}
\quad\text{on }\mathbb R^L,
\]
where \(\delta\) denotes unit point mass. Their ambient dimensions \(N_D,L\) are positive. The map to the measure notation of accepted fact b14e36d0dd8bfdb7 is \(V_1=\mathbb R^{E_D}\), \(V_2=\mathbb R^L\), \(\mu_1=\mu_D\), \(\mu_2=\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}\), \(P_1=D_D\), and \(P_2=\{-1,0,1\}^L\). Its generic points \(p_1,p_2\) are the roots \(\mathbf x,\mathbf y\), not the probability tables denoted by \(p\) here. Its \(M_i\) denote suprema of depth and are not our \(M_3\); we use the pointwise lower bound proved in its proof, not a bound on those suprema.

Because there are only finitely many halfspace traces on each finite support, the infimum defining that fact's \(h_\mu\) equals our depth minimum. Equation (6) consequently gives the exact normalization map
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_{\mu_D}(\mathbf x)&=\tau_{p_D}(\mathbf x),&
h_{\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf y)&=\tau_{p_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf y),\\
h_{\mu_D\otimes\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)
&=\tau_{p^*}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
In particular no capacity factor enters these probability-measure depths.

The pointwise argument of accepted fact b14e36d0dd8bfdb7 gives
\(h_{\mu_D\otimes\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\ge h_{\mu_D}(\mathbf x)h_{\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf y)\). To spell out its applicability to the actual caps, take any proper closed halfspace
\(H=\{(\mathbf x',\mathbf y'):\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x'+\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf y'\ge t\}\) containing \((\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\). The first-factor set \(H_D:=\{\mathbf x':\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x'+\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf y\ge t\}\) is a containing proper closed halfspace if \(\mathbf u\ne\mathbf0\), and the whole first space otherwise. Hence \(\mu_D(H_D)\ge h_{\mu_D}(\mathbf x)\). For every \(\mathbf x'\in H_D\), the second-factor section of \(H\) contains \(\mathbf y\), and is either a proper closed halfspace or the whole second space. Its mass is at least \(h_{\mu_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf y)\). Summing these section masses against the original weights of \(\mu_D\) proves the claimed product lower bound for \(H\), and then for its infimum. This is the same argument as (18)-(23) of that accepted fact, with its normals and threshold \((a,b,c)\) aliased to \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v,t)\). It uses weak inequalities throughout and retains every boundary atom.

Cube this pointwise lower bound, use (7), and sum against the original root weights from (6):
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p^*)
&\ge\sum_{\mathbf x\in D_D}\sum_{\mathbf y\in\{-1,0,1\}^L}
 p_D(\mathbf x)p_{\mathrm{loop}}(\mathbf y)
 \tau_{p_D}(\mathbf x)^3\tau_{p_{\mathrm{loop}}}(\mathbf y)^3\\
&=M_3(p_D)M_3(p_{\mathrm{loop}})
\ge\frac{8^{-(n_D+L)}}{4096}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Only the two entire groups have been combined, so this coefficient is independent of both component count and loop count.

If \(G_D\) is empty, its support in \(\mathbb R^0\) is a singleton of weight, depth, and moment \(1\). If \(L=0\), the loop group is such a singleton. When exactly one group is nonempty, the reduced law is just the nonempty group's law in the identical coordinate space, and its actual depths coincide with that law's depths. The stronger bound \(8^{-(n_D+L)}/64\) then implies (8)'s \(4096\) bound. We do not apply the positive-dimensional measure theorem to either zero-dimensional factor. If both groups are empty, the reduced law is a singleton of depth and moment \(1\), again satisfying the bound.

Finally apply accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8 to the entire chosen finite reduction sequence. Under the previously stated alias \(\mathcal L=L_{\text{20ff9a24dcb42eb8}}\), its coordinate projection \(P\) satisfies \(P\mathcal L=I\), and it supplies the bijection \(\mathcal L:D_*\to D\), the integer-kernel isomorphism, and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\boldsymbol\theta_*&=\mathcal L^T\boldsymbol\theta,& Q_*&=Q,&
p^*_{\mathbf w}&=p_{\mathcal L\mathbf w},\\
\tau_p(\mathcal L\mathbf w)&=\tau_{p^*}(\mathbf w),&
M_3(p)&=M_3(p^*),& n&=\dim\ker\widehat A_*=n_D+L.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the dimension in (8) is exactly the original cycle rank \(n\), and (8)-(9), together with the singleton cases, prove the claimed original cubic-moment bound.

Since the original \(p\) is a probability distribution on the nonempty finite set \(D\), \(M_3(p)\le\max_{\mathbf z\in D}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3\). Taking cube roots uses \(4096=16^3\) and \(8^{-n/3}=2^{-n}\), producing an actual original root \(\mathbf z^\star\) with \(\tau_p(\mathbf z^\star)\ge2^{-n}/16\). If only one group is nonempty, the same argument improves \(1/16\) to \(1/4\). If \(n=0\), (9) and the singleton convention give depth exactly \(1\), including for a forest in the original positive-dimensional edge space.

The chart objects \(\Phi_*,\Phi,\widehat D,\widehat p\) are exactly those of accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8, with its identity \(\Phi=L\Phi_*\) written here as \(\Phi=\mathcal L\Phi_*\). That fact gives saturated integer charts, \(\widehat D=\Phi_*^{-1}(D_*)=\Phi^{-1}(D)\), a full-dimensional complete support in \(\mathbb Z^n\), and identical probability tables and actual pointwise depths. It therefore transfers this same moment and root bound to the intrinsic chart without any lattice-index factor.

For the original capacities, direct normalization gives \(p=c/T\) and \(h_c=T\tau_p\). Accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8, with its unchanged capacity notation and the reconstruction alias above, also gives \(c^*_{\mathbf w}=c_{\mathcal L\mathbf w}\), \(\sum_{D_*}c^*_{\mathbf w}=T\), \(h_c(\mathcal L\mathbf w)=h_{c^*}(\mathbf w)\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}c_{\mathbf z}h_c(\mathbf z)^3
&=\sum_{\mathbf w\in D_*}c^*_{\mathbf w}h_{c^*}(\mathbf w)^3
=T^4M_3(p^*)=T^4M_3(p),\\
h_c(\mathbf z^\star)&=T\tau_p(\mathbf z^\star)
\ge\frac{T}{16}2^{-n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The lower moment estimate therefore uses exactly the original \(T^4\); the root estimate uses exactly the original \(T\). No graph operation introduces an additional factor.

In particular, any finite subdivisions of a graph in this reduced-core class can be suppressed with the stated signed tilt additions, any attached tree edges can be deleted as bridges, and independent pure cycle components, including cycles with trees attached and two-edge cycles, reduce to free loops by accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8. Their effective loop tilt is the signed sum of the original cycle-edge tilts along a chosen traversal. All such effective tilts remain unrestricted in the estimates above. Thus the number of these operations, their series lengths, and the number of independent cycle components do not alter the coefficient. The proof asserts no reduction of arbitrary graphs or arbitrary mixed-integer convex bodies to this class.
statement:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be any finite oriented loopless multigraph, allowing parallel edges and isolated vertices. Its full signed incidence matrix \(\widehat A\) has column \(\mathbf e_v-\mathbf e_u\) for an edge directed from \(u\) to \(v\). Write \(\operatorname{cc}(G)\) for the number of underlying undirected components, including isolated vertices, and put \(N:=|E|\), \(r:=|V|-\operatorname{cc}(G)\), and \(n:=N-r\). For every \(\boldsymbol\theta\in\mathbb R^E\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
D&:=\{\mathbf z\in\{-1,0,1\}^E:\widehat A\mathbf z=\mathbf0\},&
Q&:=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}e^{\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf z},&
p_{\mathbf z}&:=e^{\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf z}/Q,\\
\tau_p(\mathbf z)&:=\min_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^E\text{ a closed affine halfspace}\\\mathbf z\in H}}
\sum_{\mathbf x\in D\cap H}p_{\mathbf x},&
M_3(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every halfspace in a positive-dimensional ambient space has a nonzero normal. For a singleton law in dimension zero, depth and cubic moment are both defined to be \(1\). The objects \(G,V,E,N,r,n,\widehat A,D,Q,p,\boldsymbol\theta,\tau_p,M_3\) are exactly those of accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8; \(\operatorname{cc}(G)\) is its \(\#\operatorname{comp}(G)\). Its reconstruction map named \(L\) will be denoted \(\mathcal L\) here, because \(L\) below denotes a number of loops. This is the explicit alias \(\mathcal L=L_{\text{20ff9a24dcb42eb8}}\), with no normalization change.

Suppose some finite sequence of the following reductions produces \(G_*\). These are exactly the operations of accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8, including their tilt rules. A bridge may be deleted, retaining all other tilts and reconstructing its coordinate as zero. An isolated vertex may be discarded. At a vertex incident with exactly two distinct nonloop edges \(e,f\) and no other edge, let their other endpoints be \(u,w\), their incidence signs at that vertex be \(\varepsilon_e,\varepsilon_f\in\{-1,1\}\), and let \(\sigma:=-\varepsilon_e\varepsilon_f\). Suppress that vertex and replace the edges by an edge \(g\) with coordinate \(\xi\), reconstructing \(z_e=\xi\), \(z_f=\sigma\xi\), and assigning tilt \(\theta_g=\theta_e+\sigma\theta_f\). If \(u\ne w\), orient \(g\) from \(u\) to \(w\) when \(\varepsilon_e=1\), and oppositely when \(\varepsilon_e=-1\). If \(u=w\), retain \(g\) as a loop with incidence column zero. All unaffected coordinates and tilts are retained. A vertex incident only with one loop is not eligible for suppression.

After discarding isolated vertices, assume \(G_*\) is the disjoint union of \(L\ge0\) one-loop components and loopless connected components \(C\), each satisfying
\[
m_C:=\min_{v\in V(C)}\deg_C(v)\ge1024,
\qquad
\max_{v\in V(C)}\deg_C(v)\le2m_C.
\]
There is no bound on the number of components or loops, and no comparison is assumed between \(m_C\) for different components. Degrees count parallel edges with multiplicity. The letter \(C\) here denotes a graph component, not the convex body in the locked problem; graph degrees are unrelated to that problem's continuous dimension \(d\).

Let \(G_D=(V_D,E_D)\) be the disjoint union of all these loopless components. Define \(N_D:=|E_D|\), \(r_D:=|V_D|-\operatorname{cc}(G_D)\), and \(n_D:=N_D-r_D\), taking the empty graph to have zero components. Write \(V_*,E_*\) for the reduced vertex and edge sets, \(\widehat A_*\) for its full incidence matrix with zero loop columns, and \(\boldsymbol\theta_*\) for the tilts obtained by the specified rules. Define \(D_*:=\{\mathbf w\in\{-1,0,1\}^{E_*}:\widehat A_*\mathbf w=\mathbf0\}\), \(Q_*:=\sum_{\mathbf w\in D_*}e^{\boldsymbol\theta_*\cdot\mathbf w}\), and \(p^*_{\mathbf w}:=e^{\boldsymbol\theta_*\cdot\mathbf w}/Q_*\). These \(G_*,V_*,E_*,\widehat A_*,D_*,\boldsymbol\theta_*,Q_*,p^*\) are exactly their counterparts in accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8. Let \(\boldsymbol\theta_D\) be the restriction of \(\boldsymbol\theta_*\) to \(E_D\). Using the incidence matrix \(\widehat A_D\) of \(G_D\), put
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_D&:=\{\mathbf x\in\{-1,0,1\}^{E_D}:\widehat A_D\mathbf x=\mathbf0\},&
Q_D&:=\sum_{\mathbf x\in D_D}e^{\boldsymbol\theta_D\cdot\mathbf x},&
p_D(\mathbf x)&:=e^{\boldsymbol\theta_D\cdot\mathbf x}/Q_D.
\end{aligned}
\]
Label the free loops by \(1,\ldots,L\), write \(\theta_{*,j}\) for their reduced tilts, and define \(\boldsymbol\theta_{\mathrm{loop}}:=(\theta_{*,j})_{j=1}^L\), \(Z_j:=1+e^{\theta_{*,j}}+e^{-\theta_{*,j}}\), \(Q_{\mathrm{loop}}:=\prod_{j=1}^L Z_j\), and
\(p_{\mathrm{loop}}(\mathbf y):=\prod_{j=1}^L e^{\theta_{*,j}y_j}/Z_j\) on \(\{-1,0,1\}^L\). Empty products and the probability of the singleton empty-coordinate support equal \(1\). Define the actual depths and moments of these laws by the same \(\tau,M_3\) formulas in their respective edge-coordinate spaces.

Then \(n=n_D+L\), and the grouped bounds are
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p_D)&\ge\frac{8^{-n_D}}{64}&&\text{if }G_D\ne\varnothing,\\
M_3(p_{\mathrm{loop}})&\ge\frac{8^{-L}}{64}&&\text{if }L\ge1,\\
M_3(p)&\ge\frac{8^{-n}}{4096},&
\max_{\mathbf z\in D}\tau_p(\mathbf z)&\ge\frac{2^{-n}}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If exactly one group is nonempty, the stronger bound \(M_3(p)\ge8^{-n}/64\) holds. If \(n=0\), the original law is a singleton and its depth and moment are \(1\).

For every \(a>0\), let \(c_{\mathbf z}:=a e^{\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf z}\), \(T:=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}c_{\mathbf z}\), and \(h_c(\mathbf z):=\min_{H\ni\mathbf z}\sum_{\mathbf x\in D\cap H}c_{\mathbf x}\), with the singleton convention \(h_c=T\) in dimension zero. These are the capacity objects \(a,c,T,h_c\) of accepted fact 20ff9a24dcb42eb8. Then
\[
\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}c_{\mathbf z}h_c(\mathbf z)^3
=T^4M_3(p)\ge\frac{T^4}{4096}8^{-n},
\qquad
\max_{\mathbf z\in D}h_c(\mathbf z)\ge\frac{T}{16}2^{-n}.
\]
In particular, there is an original root \(\mathbf z^\star\in D\) such that every original closed halfspace containing it has capacity at least \(T2^{-n}/16\). All bounds hold in the saturated intrinsic lattice chart as well, with exactly the same original \(T\), no multiplicity or lattice-index factor, and all boundary atoms retained.
